findings.title: Free-shipping threshold for RO/DE subtotals of 50.00 or more is not implemented
findings.detail: The requirement states "an order to `RO` or `DE` whose subtotal is 50.00 or more ships free (fee 0.00)", but the committed function never reads `subtotal`: it looks up the country in a two-entry table and returns the fee. shipping_fee(Decimal("50.00"), "RO") therefore returns 4.99 and shipping_fee(Decimal("50.00"), "DE") returns 9.99. No criterion covers the threshold (both criteria are explicitly below it), so this is invisible to the traceability matrix and to the gate report, but it is a normative SHALL in the same requirement the implementation claims to satisfy. `subtotal` is an unused parameter, which is the direct cause.

findings.title: Negative subtotal does not raise ValueError
findings.detail: The requirement says "The subtotal is checked first: a negative subtotal SHALL raise ValueError". The committed implementation performs no subtotal check at all, so shipping_fee(Decimal("-1.00"), "RO") returns Decimal("4.99") instead of raising. "checked first" also implies ordering that the code does not implement: for an unknown country with a negative subtotal the requirement implies ValueError, while the code raises UnsupportedShippingCountry because the country lookup happens first and the subtotal is never consulted. No listed criterion covers this.

findings.title: Threshold comparison method for sub-cent subtotals is unspecified
findings.detail: Neither the requirement nor the two criteria say how a subtotal with more than two decimals is compared against 50.00: comparing the raw Decimal, or quantizing the subtotal to 0.01 first, are both reasonable and differ for values such as Decimal("49.999") (fee under the first reading, free under the second). The committed code makes no comparison at all, so it returns the flat fee for every subtotal. This input is pinned by no scenario, so it becomes a specification scenario.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN an order with a subtotal of 50.00 ships to RO THEN the shipping fee is 4.99

findings.title: Behaviour for non-finite subtotals is unspecified
findings.detail: The requirement assumes a finite Decimal subtotal and no scenario covers NaN or Infinity. Two reasonable implementations differ: one that guards the threshold comparison would raise decimal.InvalidOperation on Decimal("NaN"), one that returns the flat fee would not. The committed code ignores the subtotal, so it returns the flat fee.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN an order with a subtotal of Decimal("NaN") ships to DE THEN the shipping fee is 9.99
